title: From fixed event script to constrained trajectory model
old_model: A birth chart maps directly to a fixed sequence of future events; temporal periods are treated as event guarantees.
observed_limitations: This collapses time environment into outcome.
It cannot distinguish acquired state, personal action and external context.
It risks explaining every post-hoc outcome without a preregistered target or opportunity to fail.
current_model: Represent the natal chart as one structural prior within a broader trajectory model: S_(t+1) = F(S_t, N, E_t, A_t, C_t; θ). N is natal structure, E_t temporal environment, S_t acquired state, A_t action and C_t external context/disturbance. The equation is a research representation, not a source-given law.
rationale: The model creates separate slots for structure, environment, history, action and context, making alternative trajectories and empirical tests conceptually expressible.
consequences: Temporal environment is not an event guarantee.
Action and external context are distinct.
Any predictive value must be tested against context-only and other baselines.
Causal recommendations require separate causal identification.
what_remains_valid: Traditional source rules can still constrain the candidate interpretation space.
The model is useful as a design hypothesis even before empirical validity is established.
claim_effects: Records the current status and wording ceiling of CL-004.
boundaries: Research hypothesis / product modeling framework only.
Empirical support is currently NONE in the cited artifacts.
